title: AI-Driven Signal Scoring: LLM Analyzes Tool Output to Set Context Signals
goal: Replace hardcoded trigger signals in capabilities.json with LLM-driven analysis of tool output. After each tool completes, the existing ChatGPT OAuth provider analyzes the stdout_text and sets rich signals in the inventory snapshot signal_profile: login_form_found, upload_form_present, injectable_parameter, session_cookie_present, etc. This makes the selector adaptive rather than rule-based, and avoids the brittleness of regex-matching against JSON output.
generation_reason: Static trigger signals require manual maintenance and miss contextual evidence. The LLM can analyze httpx JSON output and identify login forms, file upload endpoints, and injectable parameters automatically.
success_criteria: After httpx runs, signals like login_form_found and session_cookie_present are automatically set from tool output.
auth-flow and session-security score higher than nikto/headers-security when login forms are detected.
No hardcoded string matching required for signal extraction.

acceptance_criteria: auth-flow scores higher after login form detected.

out_of_scope: Bypassing approval gates, scope/ROE boundaries, credential protections, or kill-switch behavior.
Running live public target scans without explicit operator authorization.
